entry_point: Every local MCP server start path: the thv run command's flag default, the workload create/edit HTTP handlers, the MCP run-server tool's config builder, replaying a saved run definition through the CLI, and replaying one through the injected API import handler

verified.entry_point: Confirmed offline at the pinned+injected commit: with no isolation option each path builds a RunConfig whose IsolateNetwork is false. CLI via AddRunFlags+buildRunnerConfig (probe: false); API create/update via WorkloadRoutes.createWorkload/updateWorkload over httptest with mocked manager and stubbed retriever/puller (probe: false); MCP run-server tool via buildServerConfig with a registered fake runtime (probe: false); CLI saved definition via runFromConfigFile with a definition that omits the field, reading the persisted state (probe: false); injected API import via importWorkloads (false). On the reference fix every one is true and every explicit opt-out stays false.

verified.services: none; the suites replace the container runtime, registry retriever and image puller with stubs and need no Docker daemon and no network at test time
verified.project_tests_run: go test pkg/api/v1 pkg/mcp/server cmd/thv/app pkg/workloads/upgrade pkg/runner — existing TestRunConfig_WriteJSON_ReadJSON and TestApplier_Apply_PreservesFullUserConfig are kept in the functional group; the published-fix update to TestRunConfigToCreateRequest is part of the reference fix because the request field becomes a pointer

wrong_fix_catalogue.refuse_all: n/a: there is no refusal on the protected path; ordinary servers must keep starting, and a fix that refuses them fails the functional suite.
wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the protection is a default value, not a refusal; a crash or 500 on a legitimate start is caught by the functional suite.
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the decision applies to the exact container being started; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource that could be authorised instead.
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: network isolation has no peer or direction dimension, and every start route is checked independently rather than by one toggle.
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the protected outcome is the network the container is started on; there is no separate read and write verb to guard.
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the protection is the value used to deploy; the saved-definition security test reads the value that is actually used, and a default applied after the definition is persisted leaves the used value wrong, so no separate patch is needed.
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the inputs are a boolean option and a serialised definition, not a parsed identity whose malformed spelling could hide it from the guard.
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: there is no external authority that could return nothing and make the default fail open.

traps.lever: reported site: the run command's isolation flag defaults off
traps.shape: start a server with no isolation option
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none — this is the site the report leads to

traps.lever: pattern A far site: the HTTP API decides the same default from its own request schema, on create and on edit
traps.shape: create and edit a workload with the field omitted
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report shows the CLI, and the edit operation reuses the create schema so a handler-level create default looks like it covers both
traps.realistic_because: real published-fix far site in a different package

traps.lever: pattern B route where the protection never existed: the MCP run-server tool builds its own run configuration
traps.shape: ask the run-server tool to start a server; its arguments carry no isolation option
traps.reason_to_dismiss: an experimental agent-facing control tool with a minimal argument set that is expected to inherit whatever the builder does; not the CLI or API the report shows
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code the published fix never touches

traps.lever: pattern B route plus a producer off the check's path: replaying a saved run definition through the CLI, whose serialised form drops an explicit false
traps.shape: start a definition that omits the setting (must isolate) and one that records an explicit opt-out after a save/export round trip (must stay off)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: a saved configuration is a complete explicit specification, so replay it literally; the producer that writes it looks like an unrelated serializer
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code the published fix never touches

traps.lever: injected sibling: the API import handler replays saved definitions through a second implementation
traps.shape: import a definition that omits the setting (must isolate) and one that explicitly disables it (must stay off)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the import endpoint is the API face of the CLI's saved-definition path, so a solver who fixed the CLI assumes the shared behaviour covers it
traps.realistic_because: ordinary maintainer code: an API face for a flow the CLI already supports; covered only by the general property

traps.lever: coupled must-keep-working: explicit opt-outs, existing settings and the save/export round trip
traps.shape: explicit false on every start path; a stored explicitly-false server whose version changes; an exported explicit-false definition
traps.reason_to_dismiss: over-hardening (forcing isolation at a shared helper) is the tempting shortcut and breaks these
traps.realistic_because: real coupled behaviour of the stored configuration and the version-change path

out_of_scope_notes: Auxiliary containers (the inspector and the embedding service) are deployed directly and are not MCP server workloads.
The Kubernetes operator does not consume the isolation option.
A permission profile that explicitly selects the host or none network mode bypasses isolation by design.
